newsitem.title: USA: Workers at GM's Saginaw plant approve contract.
newsitem.headline: Workers at GM's Saginaw plant approve contract.

text.p: Workers at General Motors Corp.'s Saginaw, Mich., foundry overwhelmingly approved a contract reached late last week with the automaker, the union said Thursday.

Local contracts at other GM plants remained unresolved, however, and 5,800 GM workers have been on strike at a Pontiac, Mich., full-size pickup truck plant since April 22 as intermittent bargaining continued.
The United Auto Workers said Wednesday night's rank-and-file vote by Local 455 resulted in an "overwhelming" approval of the contract reached late Friday.
Friday's agreement averted a threatened strike by about 900 workers at the foundry, which produces pistons, piston rods and transmission parts for a variety of GM vehicles.

The union said the automaker agreed to add 20 skilled trade jobs and 60 production positions. GM also agreed to contract language that limits outsourcing for the life of the agreement and provides job security for workers in skilled trades.
GM also agreed to pay signing bonuses to skilled trade workers worth $225,000, amounting to about $760 per person, the union said.
